summary: Nariaki Nakazato is an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD from the University of Calcutta in 1985. He held positions at Kobe University, the Toyo Bunko, and the University of Tokyo.
Narimoto Tamayama (1916–2004) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology who served as a professor at Taisho University (attested in 1974 and 1988).

Nashalla Gwyn Nyinda specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Naropa University, Chagpori Tibetan Medical Institute, Shang Shung Institute, Qinghai University, and ITEA. She became clinic director of Nyinda Clinic in 2009 and president of Chagpori in 2022.

Philosopher Natalie Depraz studied at ENS de Fontenay-Saint-Cloud and Paris Nanterre University. She has held posts at the Collège International de Philosophie, Paris-Sorbonne, University of Rouen Normandy, Paris Nanterre, and the University of Bucharest.
Natalie Gummer works in Buddhist and religious studies. She held an affiliation at Harvard University (attested 2001) and was appointed professor of religious studies at Beloit College in 2001.

Natalie Maxwell, a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin–Madison under Stephan V. Beyer, also studying under Geshe Wangyal, Khensur Ngawang Lengden, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, and Minoru Kiyota.

Natalie Quli works in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Cal Poly Humboldt and the Graduate Theological Union, she has served as Yehan Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and the Numata Center.
Natalie Rothman is a historian who completed her studies at the University of Michigan (1999–2006) and joined the University of Toronto in 2006.

Natalya Julianovna Lubotskaya (1933–1985) was an Indologist who studied at Moscow State Pedagogical University and worked as a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences from 1957 to 1976.
Natalya Mikhailovna Sazanova (1932–2006) was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied history at Moscow State University. She taught there from 1958 and became a professor in 1989.

Natalya Vasilyevna Dyakonova (1907–1996) studied at Saint Petersburg State University and worked in Iranian/Central Asian, historical, and Buddhist studies at the Ukrainian Oriental Institute, the Institute of Oriental Studies, and the State Hermitage Museum.

Natasha Heller is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies who earned her PhD from Harvard. She held posts at UC Berkeley, UCLA, and joined the University of Virginia as associate professor in 2017.

Natasha Reichle works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her dissertation at UC Berkeley under Joanna Gottfried Williams, also studying with Amin Sweeney, Lewis Lancaster, Patricia Berger, Jeffrey Alan Hadler, and Ninik Lunde.
Natasja Bosma is an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Groningen (circa 2012–2018) under the supervision of Hans T. Bakker, and held a post there during that period.

Nathan Brown (1807–1886) was a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and Japanology. Educated at Williams College and Newton Theological Institution, he founded the American Baptist Missionary Union in 1837.

Nathan Sivin (1931–2022) was a sinologist and historian educated at MIT, the Defense Language Institute, Kyoto University, and Harvard. He taught at MIT from 1966 to 1977 and later became professor at the University of Pennsylvania.

Nathan Söderblom (1866–1931) studied at Uppsala University, the Sorbonne, and EPHE. Specializing in religious and Iranian/Central Asian studies, he held professorships in history of religions at Uppsala (1901–1912) and Leipzig (1912–1914).

Nathan W. Hill is a linguist, Tibetologist, and sinologist who studied at Harvard under Leonard van der Kuijp and Jay Jasanoff. He held principal investigator posts at SOAS and Trinity College Dublin, alongside appointments at Berkeley, Oxford, and NYU.

Nathaniel Brassey Halhed (1751–1830) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Harrow School and Christ Church, Oxford. He served as an official for the East India Company and later as secretary at East India House.
Nathaniel DeWitt Garson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, having also studied under Khenpo Namdrol.
